result.rationale:
The diff confirms the inconsistency: in zoho-bigin CalendarService, refreshOAuthTokens is called with `"zoho-bigin",
      credentialId` while every other call site (google-calendar, hubspot, lark, office365, webex, zohocrm, zoomvideo) passes `credential.userId`. The sync endpoint body serializes the value as `calcomUserId`, and the webhook contract (`userId: z.number().int()` → `prisma.user.findUnique({ where: { id: reqBody.userId } })`) expects a user id. Passing a credential id means the user lookup fails (404) or mismatches, breaking Bigin credential sync.

judged_text: This call passes `credentialId` as refreshOAuthTokens' `userId: number | null` parameter — the value serialized into the sync request body as `calcomUserId` — while every other call site in this diff passes `credential.userId`. The parent application receives a credential row id where its contract expects a Cal.com user id, so Bigin sync requests cannot be mapped to a user and return the wrong user's tokens or no tokens, breaking credential sync for Zoho Bigin on every refresh.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the refresh call was changed to `refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoho-bigin", credentialId)`. The helper `refreshOAuthTokens` serializes its third argument as `calcomUserId` in the sync request body (`body: new URLSearchParams({ calcomUserId: userId.toString(), appSlug })`). Every other updated call site in this diff passes `credential.userId`, but Zoho Bigin passes `credentialId`, which (by name and typical usage in these services) is not the Cal.com user id. This would cause the sync endpoint to receive the wrong identifier and be unable to map the request to the correct user, breaking credential sync for Zoho Bigin refreshes.
